Senses.PreferredTarget: donkey lips and a horse mouth

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Donkey lips and a horse mouth join parts from two different animals into one mismatched speech-image. Chan masters use it for noisy, borrowed, or ill-fitting talk and invite anyone displaying such a mouth to come out and receive a blow.
EvidenceBody: Feiyin Tongrong says donkey lips and horse mouths all emerged at the retreat’s end.
A Five Houses record applies it to people who memorize others’ refuse and boast of many turns of questioning.
Ruibai Mingxue asks whether anyone wants to display such a mouth and calls that person out for a blow.
Xueguan Zhiyin says a style of punching, kicking, and indiscriminate ferocity ends as donkey-lips horse-mouth and public ridicule.
